description:
Every fact that the packaged profile and the adopter configuration reference restate is derived from its authority rather than kept in agreement by hand, and the binary carries mechanism and no instance of it: every declarative configuration reaches a repository as package content rather than as bytes compiled into the executable that applies it.

## Background

Three facts in this repository existed as two copies each, held correct by an assertion or by nothing at all. Two are now derived: the repository planning-bracket template declaration is generated from the packaged contribution, and the shipped documentation-policy classification reaches both the adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration by generation.

The third remains. The packaged profile embeds its whole directory into the binary at compile time, so an asset an adopter receives must live inside that directory, while this repository also consumes the same files live at their working paths. Every such asset is therefore carried twice in the tree. A test asserts each pair byte-identical, executable mode included, so drift fails the suite rather than shipping — but both copies are hand-maintained, and keeping them equal is a step a contributor must remember on every edit. That test also walks one direction only: it checks each declared asset against the live file it mirrors and never checks that a live file belonging in the package was declared, so a newly added consumer is absent from every adopter install without anything reporting it.

The owner has since ruled that domain agnosticism admits no durable exception. The template *system* is engine capability and belongs in the source; a specific application of it — this project's planning bracket — does not. `@/invariant/domain-agnostic` presently carves the planning-bracket preset trio out as its one sanctioned exception; that carve-out is removed, and the profile carrying it leaves the binary. Investigation `a62d444d` (`dev/active/a62d444d/findings.md`) established the mechanism, the ordering, and the consequences. Deriving the packaged tree and extracting the profile are one body of work: the derivation produces the artefact the extraction distributes, and doing them in either order alone leaves a structure the other removes.

The ruling reaches further than the profile. The binary also carries this repository's own documentation-area names as the classification it scaffolds into an adopter's configuration, this repository's generator-script paths and documentation targets as a generated-artifact table, this repository's git hooks as embedded scripts, and a full configuration template declaring a type hierarchy, a namespace registry, and six item kinds. Each is an instance of the mechanisms around it rather than a mechanism, so each leaves under the same principle. The audit named in D-18 establishes the complete inventory and its ordering before any of that is planned.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The adopter configuration reference and the copyable example configuration obtain the managed, permanent, and issue-scoped area lists from the packaged default profile's `[documentation]` declaration, and neither document retains a hand-maintained second copy of any of those lists.
- [hard] REQ-02: A change to either the repository planning-bracket template declaration or its packaged counterpart, without the corresponding change to the other, fails the test suite. The guard compares the two parsed declarations rather than a hand-written expectation of their contents.
- [hard] REQ-03: The packaged live-asset tree is derived from the repository files it mirrors rather than carried as a second checked-in copy, and editing a live file alone cannot leave the packaged copy stale.
- [hard] REQ-04: Two assemblies from identical sources and identical explicit environment produce identical package content, observed as an identical reported package hash, and report identical provenance.
- [hard] REQ-05: Every root the packaged live assets are drawn from is declared, and a repository file under any declared root that is neither declared as a packaged asset nor matched by a declared exclusion fails the test suite, so a new live consumer cannot be omitted from the package unnoticed.
- [hard] REQ-07: The binary compiles in no domain-specific workflow profile or preset, and `@/invariant/domain-agnostic` carries no sanctioned exception.
- [hard] REQ-08: A profile package and every package it declares a dependency on are discovered from declared repository-local locations and applied without a jit source checkout.
- [hard] REQ-09: The release that removes the embed carries the package in that same release, so no release exists in which the profile is reachable only from a source checkout.
- [hard] REQ-10: `jit validate --fix` restores profile-owned targets by re-resolving the package from the provenance record's source path, and fails loudly when it cannot resolve.

## Decisions

- D-1: The repository planning-bracket template declaration is generated from the packaged contribution, which is the authority; the repository copy is a rendered region whose freshness the test suite checks. Rejected: synchronizing the three description strings and guarding deep equality of two hand-edited copies, which leaves both hand-maintained; guarding structure alone and letting descriptions diverge, which leaves REQ-02 unmet by construction.
- D-2: The packaged live-asset inventory stays an explicit per-file declaration and gains a declared root-and-exclusion list that turns omission into a failure. Rejected: include and exclude globs replacing the inventory, because a missed exclusion over-packages an adopter install, which is worse than the omission it prevents.
- D-3: Only the `[documentation]` table of the copyable example configuration becomes generated; the rest of that file stays hand-authored, and its present illustrative subset gives way to the shipped table a fresh repository actually receives. Rejected: replacing that whole file with the initialization scaffold, which would add and remove unrelated tables for reasons this work does not decide.
- D-4: The shipped policy reaches both documents through a repository-local generator that initializes a throwaway repository and reads the table the shipped code path wrote there, verified by a mechanical freshness check. Rejected: a new command that prints the shipped policy, which adds adopter-visible surface whose only consumer is this repository's documentation pipeline; a projection over a new engine item kind, which would need a source mode for a compiled constant that no declared kind has.
- D-5: Reproducibility is observed over the package content and the reported provenance, compared across two assemblies, rather than over the produced binary's bytes. Rejected: comparing binary bytes, because the workspace has no such property today for reasons unrelated to this work — absolute paths reach debug information — so the criterion would expand into a reproducible-builds effort this work does not scope.
- D-6: Every root the live assets are drawn from is completeness-checked, so all packaged assets are covered and no root is exempt. Exclusions are glob patterns rather than path literals, since a literal list of the non-packaged files under the declared roots would itself be a hand-maintained inventory. Rejected: checking only the skill root, which leaves the remaining assets uncovered; declaring one root per skill, which relocates the same omission risk one level up.
- D-7: REQ-04 is restated over the produced package rather than the embed, and REQ-06 ("editing a live consumer alone reports a binary installed before that edit as stale") is retired rather than renumbered, so the investigation's per-criterion analysis keeps its referents. Its property survives as REQ-03's clause on packaged staleness. Rejected: dropping the reproducibility property, which leaves nothing asserting that a script-assembled package is stable across assemblies; closing the epic with both criteria undelivered, which puts a partial close in front of the holistic-review gate.
- D-8: `jit validate --fix` re-resolves a profile package from a source path carried in the provenance record at `.jit/profiles/<id>.json`, and fails loudly when that path no longer resolves. Rejected: requiring `--from` on every repair, which loses unattended repair; trusting the stored record when the package is unresolvable, which silently converts `--fix` from "restores profile-owned targets" to "restores what it can still see" and regresses `@/invariant/derived-state-coherence`.
- D-9: `@/charter/D-8` is amended narrowly to one offline profile discovered from a declared repository-local location, leaving the rest of its deferred lifecycle list intact. Rejected: leaving the charter unamended while the extraction contradicts its embedded-profile clause; reopening the deferred lifecycle generally, which admits composition, upgrade, and removal into v1.0.
- D-10: Extraction and the retargeted packaging interior are delivered inside this epic rather than as a separate container, and the epic gains criteria describing them. Rejected: a separate extraction epic, which splits one artefact's derivation from its distribution across two containers and leaves this one closing on criteria whose subject the other removes.
- D-11: The task publishing the package as a release asset is a hard predecessor of the task deleting the embed, so no release exists in which the profile is reachable only from a source checkout. Rejected: accepting a window between the two, which is the condition `@/charter/D-8`'s Rejected branch names.
- D-12: `DEFAULT_PLANNING_ROLE`, `DEFAULT_BREAKDOWN_ROLE`, and `DEFAULT_CONTAINER_ANCHOR` stay in the engine as defaults for template-mechanism parameters. The amended `@/invariant/domain-agnostic` admits mechanism-parameter defaults as engine vocabulary while excluding workflow shapes, presets, and gate bundles. Rejected: deleting them, which forces every repository to declare bindings it currently inherits without removing any workflow content from the binary.
- D-13: The binary carries no declarative configuration. Every type name, label namespace, item kind, documentation-area classification, workflow rule, and path at which the binary writes one of its own projections reaches a repository as package content or comes from the repository, whether it names this repository or is generically opinionated. Bare `jit init` writes the structural minimum, and `jit init --profile <id> --from <path>` is the populated path through the same resolver REQ-08 builds, so no separate scaffold code path remains. Rejected: exempting the generic scaffold because it names no repository, which leaves two routes into a repository for the same class of declaration; exempting only runtime-read content, which keeps this project's own area names compiled into every adopter binary.
- D-14: Two packages ship. `jit-default` carries the domain vocabulary a repository needs to be usable; `jit-dogfood` carries this project's workflow and declares a package dependency on it, resolved at application time. Composition therefore enters v1.0 and `@/charter/D-8` is amended to admit it. Rejected: each package carrying a complete copy of the shared vocabulary guarded by an equality assertion, which is the hand-maintained duplicate this epic exists to remove; generating `jit-default` from `jit-dogfood`, which makes the generic package a derivative of one project's workflow.
- D-15: REQ-01's authority moves from the compiled documentation-policy constant to the packaged default profile's `[documentation]` declaration; the delivered generator keeps its shape — it initializes a throwaway repository and reads what the shipped path wrote — and changes only what it reads. The criterion is restated when the constant's removal is planned, not before, so it continues to describe what is delivered. Rejected: striking REQ-01, which leaves the adopter documents with a hand-maintained area list again; exempting the constant from this pass, which ships this project's own area names to every adopter through v1.0.
- D-16: The release archive carries both package directories alongside the binaries, so an adopter who unpacks one download can initialize offline with no second fetch. Rejected: separate per-package release assets, which cost the self-contained install property `docs/reference/profiles.md` promises; placing a package at a machine-level location during install, which makes a repository's derived-state repair depend on machine state against `@/charter/D-1` and reopens the search-path precedence `@/charter/D-8` defers.
- D-17: The registry-derived default rules — `label-format`, `namespace-registry`, `type-hierarchy-known`, and `namespace-unique-<ns>` — stay in the engine as mechanism over whatever registry the adopter declares. That property holds only once the compiled taxonomy defaults are removed: today three `Default` impls supply a registry and a hierarchy when the adopter declares neither, so a repository declaring nothing still receives seven rules and their JSON-Schema projections over names it never wrote. Removing those defaults is the precondition that makes this decision demonstrable rather than aspirational. `orphan-leaf` and `strategic-consistency` encode a workflow opinion and move to `jit-dogfood`. Rejected: moving every rule, which leaves a repository unable to validate a label until it has applied a package.
- D-18: An audit inside this epic inventories every remaining embedded configuration against D-13's boundary and returns a sequenced recommendation before any of it is planned. Fan-out blocks on it. Rejected: planning the cleanup directly from this session's inventory, which was assembled by grep and is not a basis for sequencing a change of this size.
- D-19: The resolver ships with no runtime compatibility check; a package's declared version requirement is parsed and not matched against the running binary. REQ-09 states the property D-11 and D-16 protect — that no release exists in which the profile is reachable only from a source checkout — rather than fixing the delivery shape as a separate asset. Accepted consequence: a package built for a later binary applies cleanly and fails wherever the shape later differs. The check belongs to the profile lifecycle `@/charter/D-8` defers. Rejected: amending REQ-08 to require the match, and adding a criterion of its own, both of which pull an unbuilt `VersionReq::matches` and its typed error into this container.
- D-20: `jit-default` declares all six item kinds, and no package names a source file no repository has. The rule and gate registries already exist in a freshly initialized repository — one seeded, one empty — and the invariant registry does not, only because initialization never creates it. Initialization creates it the way it creates the gate registry, so `invariant` is default vocabulary like the rest, and `jit-dogfood` contributes its invariant entries into that registry instead of publishing the file over it. Rejected: leaving `invariant` to the workflow package, which makes a core addressable kind reachable only by applying this project's own workflow; declaring it in `jit-default` while the file may be absent, which is the dangling declaration the rule exists to prevent; a two-kind `jit-default`, which makes an adopter declare the kinds needed to address their own gates and rules.
- D-21: The boundary reaches this repository's own path constants. No adopter binary names a path inside this checkout: the projection targets and generator commands at `output.rs`, `schema.rs`, `storage/reference.rs`, `domain/event_catalog.rs`, `runtime_defaults.rs`, and `gate_presets/reference.rs` each move behind a repository-supplied value or a test-support boundary, and D-13's enumeration carries the corresponding class. Rejected: treating them as outside the boundary because they are written into no repository, which leaves six of this checkout's paths in every adopter binary; deferring the decision, which invites a later reviewer to read the residue as an omission from D-13.
- D-22: The four named icon presets are deleted rather than moved, since the per-type `custom` map already expresses any of them and deletion removes no capability; the accepted consequence is that `GET /config/hierarchy` answers differently for a repository that set one. The git hook scripts stay in the engine as lease and branch-drift enforcement mechanism, and the stale path inside `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` is a defect filed on its own. Rejected: moving both to a package, which makes `jit hooks install` require an applied package before it has anything to install; keeping the presets, which leaves four named domain vocabularies compiled in.
- D-23: The unreachable item-kind defaults at `domain/item.rs` are deleted rather than retained. No adopter declaration reaches them — a partial `[item_kinds.X]` table is rejected at load and an absent table yields an empty kind set — so deletion is behaviour-preserving and removes three domain-vocabulary literals. Rejected: retaining them as D-12-class mechanism-parameter defaults, which leaves unreachable constants standing against `@/invariant/canonical-cutover`.

## Notes

REQ-03 and REQ-07 both change what the binary contains, so every downstream verdict rebuilds once they land.

The assembly's ordering risk changes shape across this work. While the package is still embedded, a derivation that runs after the embedding macro produces a silently stale binary rather than an error; once the embed is gone, the assembly's output is the distribution artefact and the ordering constraint is against publication rather than compilation. Either way the directory the derivation writes into is not reset between runs, so a live consumer that is deleted or renamed leaves its stale copy behind and ships unless the derivation reconciles the directory it owns.

An earlier epic weighed and rejected build-time generation of this package tree, and made the package the authority with the live paths as its rendered consumers. The renderer that decision assumed was never built, which is why the tree carries hand-maintained duplicates today. This work supersedes both positions.

Upholds `@/invariant/single-source-prose`, `@/invariant/canonical-cutover`, `@/invariant/domain-agnostic`, and `@/invariant/bounded-rust-build-footprint`.
title: Derived profile assets and projected policy documentation
